{{nihongo|'''Tomi Shrine'''|等彌神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Tomi Shrine''' (とみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|Q127026|qid=Q127026}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|Q131287|qid=Q131287}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} (small), and its former rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}. It is identified with the '''Tomi Shrine''' of Shikinokami District, {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}}, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}. Until the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period it was called '''Notomiya'''.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown, but according to shrine tradition this shrine was originally located on {{ill|Mount Torimi|Q18700112|qid=Q18700112}}. Torimiyama is said to be the sacred ritual ground (matsuriniwa) where {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|Q200188|qid=Q200188}}, Japan's first {{ill|Emperor of Japan|Q208233|qid=Q208233}}, worshipped the imperial ancestral deities and heavenly deities in spring, second month, of his fourth regnal year after enthronement<ref>''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}'', volume 3.</ref>. The Nihon Shoki account that he first worshipped the imperial ancestral deities after enthronement is also considered the origin and first stage of the {{ill|Daijosai|Q11433653|qid=Q11433653|lt=Daijōe}}.

The deity of Kamitsuo-sha, which corresponds to the main shrine, is given as {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Ōhirume-no-Muchi-no-Mikoto}}, though there is also a theory that it is {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054|lt=Nigihayahi-no-Mikoto}}.

In the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} it was listed as a shikinaisha, but in {{ill|Ten'ei|Q1193915|qid=Q1193915}} 3 ({{ill|1112|Q19525|qid=Q19525}}), a landslide caused the shrine buildings to be moved to the present location.

In {{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 15), it was promoted from village shrine to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural Shrine}}.

In the 1950s, {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|Q127026|qid=Q127026}} {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|Q1534477|qid=Q1534477}} was founded in the precincts.

There are 13 stone monuments in the precincts (Man'yō poem monuments, haiku monuments, and waka monuments).

A distinctive feature of this shrine is that its {{ill|Yatagarasu|Q745463|qid=Q745463}} is depicted in human form.

===  Access ===
* About 15 minutes on foot from {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125|lt=JR West}} / {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|Q1531085|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu}} {{ill|Sakurai Station (Nara)|Q5361714|qid=Q5361714|lt=Sakurai Station}}
* From JR/Kintetsu Sakurai Station, bus for {{ill|Tanzan Shrine|Q488618|qid=Q488618}}, get off at "Kaminomori-chō," then 2 minutes on foot
